main_text.p: hoftium loco habentur, idque ex ordine. Unde etiam Titus Manlius, poft Torquatus, cum à Gallo provocaretur, Dicta-torem ita allocutus est: Injussu tuo Imperator extra ordinem non pugnaverim, non si certam victoriam agnoverim: si tu permittis, ero provocatus.

Etsi vero permultis in locisBoekel. disquif. Public. judic.6. talia duella superiorum auctoritate fuerint permissa, etiam inter socios, & subditos; probanda tamen mihi videntur Hispanorum statuta, quibus nulla censetur justa duelli causa. Eaque confentanea omni1. 4. Cod. de leg. juri tam humano, quam divino. Jura equidem civilia, quae Principem secundum leges, agere debere judicant, ejusque auctoritatem à juris pendere auctoritate; nolint ea omnia justa & legitima esse, quae Princeps quoquo modo probaverit, aut permiserit. page.notes: The scan shows a faint mark or ornament at the bottom centre, not clearly a gathering signature, so it is left out. The marginal note "Boekel. disquif. Public. judic.6." consists of several short lines, the first two and the last two set in a stacked arrangement; they are given here as one note. The "ct" in "auctoritate" appears as a ligature, transcribed as "ct". The text has no printing errors I could identify.
